items.title: Produce the account aggregator readiness assessment and consent artefact design
items.outcome: A dated assessment states whether to pursue aggregator connectivity, what role and obligations it entails, what it costs, how consent artefacts map onto the existing consent ledger, and the criteria under which the work is abandoned.
items.context: Aggregator connectivity is currently a deferred assumption with no owner, which is the state most likely to produce an expensive surprise later. Writing the assessment converts it into a decision that can be made, revisited or dropped deliberately.
scope: Role and obligation analysis for participation, including the licensing position
Cost model covering integration, ongoing fees and operational burden
Consent artefact model mapped onto the existing consent ledger and purpose registry
Data minimisation, retention and purpose limitation position for fetched data
Named abandon criteria and a review date
Comparison against continuing with deterministic capture alone
acceptance_criteria: The assessment states pursue or defer with a date and a named owner
Consent artefacts map onto the existing ledger without a parallel consent system
The retention position for fetched data is stated and is consistent with the existing schedule
Abandon criteria are specific enough to be evaluated without reopening the analysis
The cost model is dated and its sources are cited rather than assumed
The assessment states what capability is lost by deferring
contracts_schema: Defines the consent artefact fields the implementation ticket must carry
security_privacy: States what data would be received, from whom, and under what basis
States that the arrangement never involves holding or moving funds
observability: Names the metrics that would show whether the integration is worth its cost
tests: Review against the existing consent ledger design to confirm no parallel system is needed
rollout_rollback: Adopted on merge; the review date is tracked and the decision is revisited rather than assumed
non_goals: Implementation, which is the separate api ticket
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Owns the assessment. The implementation ticket may not start until this is accepted.
definition_of_done: Document merged and dated, with the option chosen and the options rejected recorded
Linked from every epic and ticket it unblocks
Reviewed through a current-head core-reviewer attestation from a separate qualified reviewer-agent session
Follow-up implementation tickets created or updated to reference it
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Implement aggregator consent, fetch and mapping behind a default-off kill switch
items.outcome: Aggregator consent, data fetch, mapping into the ledger and revocation are implemented as an inert capability that does nothing until a deliberate, audited configuration change enables it.
items.context: Building this behind a kill switch means the option can be exercised quickly if the assessment says pursue, without the risk of a half-finished integration touching real data in the meantime. It also forces the consent and retention semantics to be correct before anything is fetched.
scope: Consent request, artefact storage and expiry aligned with the existing consent ledger
Fetch scheduling with the minimum data scope the consent permits
Mapping of fetched records onto accounts and the ledger through the existing precedence rules
Revocation that stops fetching and removes derived records within the published window
Default-off kill switch whose state is audited
Retention and expiry of aggregator-sourced records tied to the consent artefact
acceptance_criteria: With the switch off, no aggregator code path executes and no outbound call is made, proven by a test
Enabling the switch is an audited configuration change, not a code deploy
Fetched records carry their consent artefact identifier and expire with the consent
Revoking consent stops fetching immediately and removes derived records within the published window
Fetched records deduplicate against existing sources through the shared precedence rules
No data is fetched beyond the scope the consent artefact permits, enforced in code rather than by configuration
contracts_schema: Implements the aggregator additions to the published ingestion contract as an additive registration
security_privacy: Aggregator credentials and artefacts are stored encrypted and are never logged
Fetched data is subject to the same encryption and retention rules as all other financial data
observability: Publishes fetch counts, consent expiry events and revocation outcomes without content
tests: Kill switch off path test proving no execution
rollout_rollback: Default off; enabling is per cohort and reversible without a deploy
Rollback flips the switch off and stops fetching; already mapped records remain valid
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the connector, consent handling and mapping. Client surfaces are deliberately out of scope until the assessment says pursue.
definition_of_done: Merged only after a current-head core-reviewer attestation from a separate qualified reviewer-agent session
Every acceptance criterion demonstrated by a named automated test or attached evidence
Tests listed in this ticket run in CI and are required by branch protection
Observability, rollout and rollback notes recorded on the ticket before merge
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges
